title: Packaging & Processing Lead
summary: One landed cost up front — duty, handling, final mile. If a surcharge appears, it's ours to absorb.
overview:
Job Description

This Packaging & Processing Lead position sits on the inbound and retail-processing side of our New York operation. Where the export floor protects cargo for a voyage, this role prepares received goods for onward retail and e-commerce channels — kitting, relabelling, quality inspection and repack — and leads the team that turns bulk receipts into retail-ready units.

Job responsibilities

  • Lead inbound processing: inspection, sortation, kitting and repack.
  • Own retail compliance — barcodes, price tickets, country-of-origin and safety labelling.
  • Build and maintain standard work instructions for every client programme.
  • Manage line balancing and staffing to hit daily throughput targets.
  • Run quality gates and hold anything that fails client specification.
  • Coordinate with inventory control on receipt discrepancies and disposition.
  • Track labour cost per unit and drive it down without loss of quality.
  • Onboard new client programmes from first pilot run to steady state.

Retail chargebacks come from small, repeatable mistakes. This role exists to make the correct method the easiest one to follow.

Qualification

  • 5+ years in value-added services, co-packing or retail processing, including team leadership.
  • Familiar with major retailer routing guides and labelling requirements.
  • Comfortable designing a line layout and timing a standard work cycle.
  • Strong quality discipline and willingness to stop a line when specification is not met.
  • Experience onboarding new client programmes is a strong advantage.

Duties

  • Deliver daily processed-unit targets against the client service level agreement.
  • Maintain documented standard work and revision control for each programme.
  • Own quality escapes end to end, including client communication.
  • Report labour productivity and cost per unit weekly.
  • Develop the team through cross-training and clear progression standards.

‍

Conclusion

Processing work rewards people who care about the hundredth unit as much as the first. If that sounds like you rather than a burden, we would like to meet you.

seo.metaTitle: Packaging & Processing Lead — Retail, New York
seo.metaDescription: Full-time role leading inbound retail processing in New York — kitting, relabelling, quality gates and routing-guide compliance that prevents chargebacks.

title: Customs Broker
summary: One landed cost up front — duty, handling, final mile. If a surcharge appears, it's ours to absorb.
overview:
Job Description

The Customs Broker is the person standing between a shipment and a hold. Licensed and based in New York, this role classifies goods, files entries, manages duty and tax exposure, and answers to the authorities on our clients' behalf. Every declaration carries our name and our clients' compliance record, so accuracy here is not a preference — it is the job.

Job responsibilities

  • Classify goods under the HTS and record the reasoning behind every code.
  • File import entries and ISF within the statutory window, every time.
  • Manage customs value, duty, VAT and preference claims on each shipment.
  • Respond to holds, exams and partner agency requests for information.
  • Keep client compliance manuals and classification databases current.
  • Support audits and self-assessment reviews with retrievable records.
  • Advise coordinators on documentation that prevents avoidable holds.
  • Liaise with CBP and government agencies on our clients' behalf.

Clearance problems are almost always born upstream, in a description that was too vague or a document that arrived too late. The value of this role is in catching those before the vessel sails.

Qualification

  • Licensed Customs Broker, or actively pursuing the licence with 3+ years of entry experience.
  • Deep working knowledge of HTS classification and valuation methodology.
  • Familiar with ACE, ABI and partner government agency filing requirements.
  • Precise written communication — rulings and protests are won on wording.
  • Calm under audit and comfortable saying no to a client when the entry does not support it.

Duties

  • File every entry within the statutory window and track release status to conclusion.
  • Own the response to holds, exams and requests for information.
  • Keep client compliance manuals and classification databases current.
  • Support internal audits and periodic self-assessment reviews.
  • Train coordinators on documentation standards that prevent avoidable holds.

‍

Conclusion

A clean entry is invisible; a wrong one is expensive for years. If you would rather spend an extra hour on a classification than a month on a protest, you will fit here.

seo.metaDescription: Licensed customs broker role in New York: HTS classification, entry and ISF filing, duty exposure, and CBP liaison on holds, exams and agency queries.

title: Software Engineer
summary: Work on exciting projects with cutting-edge technology. Contribute to software development and architecture.
overview:
Job Description

The Software Engineer builds the systems our coordinators, clearance team and customers actually work in — tracking, rating, document handling and the integrations that connect carriers, customs brokers and warehouse systems. This is a contract engagement based in Chicago, working close to operations rather than at a distance from them.

Job responsibilities

  • Build and maintain backend services for tracking, rating and documents.
  • Integrate carrier, customs broker and warehouse systems, legacy EDI included.
  • Model freight data so milestones, rates and documents stay consistent.
  • Design APIs that tolerate third-party systems behaving badly.
  • Keep production reliable, observable and safe to deploy on a busy day.
  • Migrate legacy integrations without interrupting live shipments.
  • Record architecture decisions and the reasoning behind them.
  • Hand over documented, maintainable code at the end of the engagement.

Logistics software fails in unglamorous ways — a missing milestone, a duplicated document, a rate that quietly went stale. The value of this role is in noticing those failure modes before a customer does.

Qualification

  • 4+ years building production backend services.
  • Strong SQL and relational data modelling; event-driven experience welcome.
  • Practical API design skills and patience for third-party integrations that misbehave.
  • Comfortable with cloud infrastructure, CI and observability tooling.
  • Bonus: exposure to EDI, freight rating, or customs data formats.

Duties

  • Deliver against an agreed contract scope with regular, reviewable increments.
  • Keep production reliable and on-call handovers clean.
  • Migrate legacy integrations without interrupting live shipments.
  • Contribute to architecture decisions and record the reasoning.
  • Hand over documented, maintainable code at the end of the engagement.

‍

Conclusion

Freight is a domain where correctness has a shipping cost attached. If you like problems where the feedback loop is measured in containers rather than clicks, you will enjoy this one.

seo.metaDescription: Contract backend role in Chicago building tracking, rating and document services, and integrating carrier, customs and warehouse APIs including legacy EDI.

title: Packaging & Processing Lead
summary: One landed cost up front — duty, handling, final mile. If a surcharge appears, it's ours to absorb.
overview:
Job Description

The Packaging & Processing Lead runs the export packing floor in New York. This role decides how cargo is protected for the journey it is actually going to take — crating, palletising, dunnage, moisture control and marking — and leads the team that does it. Get it right and the goods arrive as they left; get it wrong and the claim lands on us.

Job responsibilities

  • Specify how each shipment is crated, palletised and secured for its route.
  • Lead the export packing team and set the daily release plan.
  • Apply ISPM 15, dangerous goods and load-securement standards on every build.
  • Select dunnage, desiccants and moisture barriers to suit transit conditions.
  • Mark and document cargo so it survives handling and inspection alike.
  • Run damage-claim root cause analysis and close out corrective actions.
  • Control material consumption and cost per shipment against budget.
  • Train new packers and sign off their first solo crates.

Packing is the last engineering decision made about a shipment. This role owns that decision and the evidence behind it.

Qualification

  • 5+ years in export packing, crating or industrial packaging, including 2+ leading a team.
  • Working knowledge of ISPM 15, dangerous goods marking and load-securement standards.
  • Able to read dimensions and weights and design a crate that survives handling.
  • Practical experience with desiccants, VCI film and moisture barrier bags.
  • Forklift certified; comfortable with power tools and packing machinery.

Duties

  • Publish and maintain the packing specification library by commodity.
  • Meet daily export release targets without compromising protection standards.
  • Keep material consumption and cost per shipment within budget.
  • Own damage-claim root cause analysis and corrective actions.
  • Train new packers and sign off on their first solo crates.

‍

Conclusion

Nobody thanks you for a crate that held. That is the point. If you take satisfaction in cargo that arrives exactly as it left, this floor is yours to run.

seo.metaTitle: Packaging & Processing Lead — Export, New York
seo.metaDescription: Full-time role leading our New York export packing floor — crating, dunnage, ISPM 15 compliance and load securement for heavy and irregular cargo.

title: Digital Marketing Specialist
summary: Develop and execute digital marketing strategies to drive brand awareness and engagement. Analyze campaign performance.
overview:
Job Description

The Digital Marketing Specialist tells the freight story to people who have been trained to expect opacity. Working part-time from San Francisco alongside commercial and operations teams, this role builds the demand engine — search, email, paid and content — that brings shippers to CargoHype and keeps them engaged between quotes.

Job responsibilities

  • Own the quarterly campaign calendar across search, paid, email and content.
  • Run SEO for the site — keyword mapping, on-page work and technical fixes.
  • Build nurture sequences that hold up in front of a sceptical freight buyer.
  • Manage paid budgets against cost per qualified lead, not impressions.
  • Write campaign copy in-house rather than waiting on an agency.
  • Report weekly on spend, pipeline influenced and attribution assumptions.
  • Keep every public claim traceable to a real operational number.
  • Partner with sales on messaging and objection handling for live deals.

Logistics buyers are sceptical for good reason. The work here is to be specific, verifiable and useful — and to let the operational numbers carry the argument.

Qualification

  • 3+ years in B2B digital marketing, ideally in logistics, supply chain or industrial services.
  • Hands-on with SEO tooling, marketing automation and paid platforms.
  • Comfortable reading an analytics funnel and defending an attribution model.
  • Strong writer — able to draft campaign copy without waiting on an agency.
  • Bonus: familiarity with freight terminology and Incoterms.

Duties

  • Deliver the quarterly campaign calendar and keep it on schedule.
  • Report weekly on spend, cost per qualified lead and pipeline influenced.
  • Maintain the content backlog and publish on cadence.
  • Partner with sales on messaging that survives first contact with a shipper.
  • Keep every public claim traceable to an operational source.

‍

Conclusion

Freight marketing is won by whoever is willing to be concrete. If you would rather publish a real transit table than another stock photo of a container ship, we should talk.

seo.metaDescription: Part-time B2B marketing role in San Francisco running search, paid, email and content — turning real transit and clearance numbers into credible campaigns.

title: Inventory Controller
summary: One landed cost up front — duty, handling, final mile. If a surcharge appears, it's ours to absorb.
overview:
Job Description

The Inventory Controller owns the truth about what we hold, where it sits and what it is worth. Based at our Austin facility on night shift, this role runs cycle counts, investigates variances and keeps system stock and physical stock in agreement — so that sales can promise, planners can plan and finance can close the month without surprises.

Job responsibilities

  • Run the rolling cycle-count calendar across every rack and bulk area.
  • Investigate each variance to root cause before any adjustment is posted.
  • Keep location, lot and batch integrity accurate in the WMS at all times.
  • Reconcile system stock to physical stock ahead of every month-end close.
  • Own inventory adjustments with a documented approval trail per write-off.
  • Maintain bonded and duty-suspended stock records to audit standard.
  • Flag ageing, slow-moving and damaged stock for disposition decisions.
  • Recommend slotting and min-max changes that cut touches and shrinkage.

Inventory accuracy is not a reporting exercise; it is the foundation every downstream commitment rests on. This role is measured on how rarely anyone downstream has to ask whether the number can be trusted.

Qualification

  • 3+ years in inventory control, stock accounting or warehouse administration.
  • Advanced spreadsheet skills and confidence with WMS or ERP inventory modules.
  • Understanding of bonded and duty-suspended stock treatment is a strong advantage.
  • Investigative mindset — comfortable chasing a discrepancy through paperwork and pallets alike.
  • Available for night-shift working and month-end close cycles.

Duties

  • Publish daily count results and variance root causes to the operations lead.
  • Maintain location and lot integrity across all racking and bulk areas.
  • Own inventory adjustments, with a documented approval trail for every write-off.
  • Support customs and audit queries with clean, retrievable stock records.
  • Recommend slotting and min-max changes that reduce touch counts and ageing.

‍

Conclusion

If you believe a stock figure should be defensible line by line, and you would rather find the cause than post the adjustment, this is the seat for you.

seo.metaDescription: Night-shift role in Austin running cycle counts, investigating variances to root cause and keeping WMS, ERP and bonded stock records in agreement.

title: Fulfillment Specialist
summary: Collaborate with cross-functional teams to create user-centered designs. Conduct user research and usability testing.
overview:
Job Description

The Fulfillment Specialist keeps the last hundred metres of the supply chain honest. Working out of our Los Angeles hub, this role picks, packs, verifies and dispatches customer orders against same-day cut-offs, and owns the accuracy of every carton that leaves the floor. When a shipment is short, mislabelled or late, the Fulfillment Specialist is the person who catches it before the customer does.

Job responsibilities

  • Pick, pack and verify customer orders against the daily dispatch plan.
  • Meet the 16:00 carrier cut-off and escalate anything that threatens it.
  • Check every carton for count, condition and labelling before it is sealed.
  • Apply carrier labels and complete manifests ahead of each pickup.
  • Run cycle counts in your zones and report variances the same shift.
  • Keep pack stations stocked, clean and laid out for the shift's volume.
  • Process returns — inspect, grade, and restock or quarantine each unit.
  • Support peak waves, including overtime and weekend dispatch when volume demands it.

Fulfillment is where promises become parcels. This role sits at the point the customer actually experiences, and the standard is simple: the right item, packed well, out the door on time, every time.

Qualification

  • 2+ years in a warehouse, 3PL or e-commerce fulfillment environment.
  • Comfortable with WMS and handheld scanning systems; barcode and RF experience preferred.
  • Able to lift 20kg repeatedly and stay on your feet through a full shift.
  • Strong numeracy and a genuine intolerance for guesswork on counts.
  • Familiar with carrier labelling requirements for parcel and LTL.
  • Forklift or pallet-jack certification is a plus.

Duties

  • Execute the daily pick-pack-ship plan and escalate anything that puts the cut-off at risk.
  • Maintain inventory accuracy in your zones through disciplined cycle counting.
  • Complete carrier manifests and shipping paperwork before pickup.
  • Support peak-season ramp-ups, including overtime and weekend waves when volume demands it.
  • Contribute to continuous-improvement reviews on packing materials, dunnage and station layout.

‍

Conclusion

A carton either arrives complete or it does not — there is no partial credit in fulfillment. If you take quiet pride in a clean pack, an accurate count and a dock that clears before the cut-off, you will do well here.

seo.metaDescription: Day-shift role in our Los Angeles hub picking, packing and dispatching orders against a 16:00 carrier cut-off, with cycle counts reconciled the same shift.

title: Transportation Coordinator
summary: One landed cost up front — duty, handling, final mile. If a surcharge appears, it's ours to absorb.
overview:
Job Description

The Transportation Coordinator is a crucial role in the logistics and supply chain industry. This position is responsible for managing and coordinating the movement of goods from suppliers to customers, ensuring that shipments are timely, cost-effective, and meet all necessary regulations. Transportation Coordinators play a key role in optimizing transportation routes and ensuring the smooth flow of products through the supply chain.

Job responsibilities

  • Plan and book daily line-haul and final-mile movements across assigned lanes.
  • Select carriers on cost, transit time and service history rather than habit.
  • Raise and check bills of lading, delivery notes and export documentation.
  • Track shipments leg by leg and flag delays before the customer notices them.
  • Reconcile carrier invoices against quoted rates and query every discrepancy.
  • Keep customers updated with milestones, not excuses, when a plan changes.
  • Maintain accurate shipment records in the tracking platform each shift.
  • Support the network desk on rebookings whenever a connection is missed.

The Transportation Coordinator plays a pivotal role in ensuring the efficient movement of goods through the supply chain. They are responsible for managing logistics, maintaining customer satisfaction, and optimizing transportation costs, making this role indispensable in the world of logistics and supply chain management.

Qualification

  • Must be familiar with military standards and regulations governing logistics policies and procedures.
  • Knowledge of the DoD systems acquisition process will be required in order to successfully adhere to doctrine and operations concepts.
  • Expertise is required in expediting hardware through the repair process to reach end users in worldwide locations.
  • Shall have familiarity with stock listing, disposal, and re- procurement processes and guidelines. Expertise in requirements computations and the use of AFLCMC/HNC CLASS is required.
  • 5 years min exp.

Duties

  • Provide logistics support for life-cycle sustainment for fielded systems used in support of TAP mission systems and equipment.
  • Duties will also include performing tasks associated with supply, procurement, sparing, logistics planning and item management.
  • Shall process field requests, repair actions and shipments within the appropriate required time frames.
  • In addition to deliverable reports, support personnel are required to input data to Government produced reports, data systems, and briefings.

‍

Conclusion

When a production line is waiting or a launch date is fixed, the plan matters more than the plane. We hold allocations with core carriers out of Dhaka and Singapore, build consolidations daily, and hand cargo to our own clearance team before wheels touch down.

seo.metaDescription: Internship in Boston planning routes, selecting carriers and tracking shipments end to end. Own the documentation and customer updates behind every move.
